text.p: The following are top headlines from selected Canadian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Shooting heats up Korean standoff: Attack on prominent defector raises tension outside consulate where Hwang is stranded.
- APEC summit agenda ignores rights: Issue too delicate, host Canada says.
- Crees, soldiers unite against chill: The army combat engineers had never experienced cold like it but the Crees showed them how to cope.
- Birth of Metro Toronto hurt too: Fifties federation a compromise.
- Re-election hopes ride on budget: Liberal strategy counts on new spending for pet causes.
- Canadian's role in Peruvian crisis grows: Canadian Ambassador Anthony Vincent among those making proposals to keep Peru, rebels talking.
- Ottawa cuts market debt: Government quietly reduces what it owes people who have invested in bonds and T-bills.
- Telecom pact widens access to the world: Canadian firms eye C$880-billion market, critics question benefit to consumers.
- Experts' pessimism on bonds waning: Market pros still are not bullish on bonds but the pessimism is waning.
- Clifford Frame back in the game: The former Curragh chairman decided a life of leisure wasn't his style and is now at the helm of Mineral Resources.
- Merger creates paper giant: Stock swap will turn Abitibi-Stone into C$4.1 billion company -- the world's largest newsprint producer.
- Barrick Gold Corp close to losing grip on Busang.
